assessment.nobel_worthiness: Foundational formal analysis of how organised interests shape trade policy (the protection-for-sale framework), together with their joint work on innovation, growth and trade. The ideas have shaped both theory and empirical work on trade policy and political economy. The work is general, conceptually clear and widely applied.
assessment.attribution: The two are the clear and well-recognised joint authors of the core political-economy-of-protection and trade-and-growth framework. Helpman is also credited in other trade entries, but his contribution here is central and attribution is clean.
assessment.maturity: Core results date from the early 1990s and have been tested, extended and absorbed into textbooks for three decades. This is a very mature, long-standing candidacy.
uncertainties: Empirical support for the protection-for-sale predictions is mixed, which could weigh against the political-economy strand.
Committee may prefer to anchor a trade prize on a different strand, such as firm heterogeneity (Melitz) or quantitative models, which would change the credited set.
Assessment rests on general knowledge; no independent verification of citation or impact data was done.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the trade-shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers understand labour demand, wage inequality and the local costs of import competition. Combines credible research designs with conceptual framing, and has large policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task framework and the China-shock work. Hanson is central to the trade-shock and local labour market evidence. Dorn is a key co-author of the China-shock papers, and Katz has major prior contributions on the skill premium, so the set is crowded and the cut is uncertain. Acemoglu's earlier recognition covers related theory of directed technology.
assessment.maturity: Task framework dates from about 2003 and the China-shock papers from 2013 onward. This is enough time for replication and debate, and the revisions of the findings are now part of the literature.
uncertainties: Findings on the persistence and size of trade-shock effects have been debated and refined.
Whether to credit Dorn or Katz instead of or alongside the two named is unclear.
Partial overlap with the 2024 prize on technology and institutions may affect committee appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Built the modern formal and empirical political economics of electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal policy. The work links political institutions to economic outcomes and has opened a large research field. It is assessed here under the same criteria as other fields, on its demonstrated influence on economics and its general importance.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the co-authors of the main synthesis and the central empirical constitutional work. Besley has strong separate claims (state capacity, accountability) and is the main alternative or addition, so the choice between two and three is a real attribution question.
assessment.maturity: Core work spans from the 1990s to the 2000s, with large follow-on literature and replication, so the timing is mature.
uncertainties: Disclosure: Persson is a long-time collaborator in the corruption and quality-of-government literature and a colleague at Stockholm University, so this member's assessment may be affected.
Cross-country institutional evidence raises identification concerns and overlaps conceptually with the 2024 prize.
Whether Besley should be included as a third laureate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model is a canonical building block of game theory and applied theory, used in labour, trade, political and market-design modelling. It offers a precise strategic foundation for outcomes such as the Nash bargaining solution.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein's 1982 paper is the identifiable core contribution. Binmore and Wolinsky add to the strategic and market-bargaining strands but are less clearly necessary, so a single-laureate proposal is most defensible.
assessment.maturity: More than four decades of use and extension. Very mature. Game theory has been recognised before (Nash, Harsanyi, Selten, Aumann, Schelling, Myerson and others), so the field is not novel for the committee.
uncertainties: Rubinstein's profile also spans bounded rationality and economic theory more broadly, so framing the prize on bargaining alone may be narrow.
Committee may judge that bargaining is already substantially recognised through mechanism design and market-design awards.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reconstructed long-run series of top incomes and wealth from tax records, which redirected economic and public debate on inequality. The data contribution is large and influential, and the work has stimulated further research on taxation and distribution.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top-income series, and Zucman is the key contributor on offshore wealth and distributional accounts. Piketty's theory of capital returns is more contested than his data work, so the credit should be weighted to measurement.
assessment.maturity: Top-income work dates from about 2003, with later book-length syntheses and wealth-tax proposals. The data are broadly accepted but remain debated.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes about wealth and income measurement, including treatment of transfers and taxes.
Public and policy prominence may be conflated with scientific contribution; r>g theory is contested.
Choice of two versus three laureates, including whether Zucman's more recent work is mature enough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Information design and Bayesian persuasion extend mechanism design by analysing how an information provider can shape beliefs. The framework has application in markets, platforms, regulation and political settings, and is conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow wrote the canonical persuasion paper, while Bergemann and Morris developed the robust mechanism design and information design lines. This is a multi-strand literature, so credit allocation is the main difficulty and Gentzkow is excluded here only for the three-name cap.
assessment.maturity: Core papers date from 2011 onward, with a robust theoretical literature but fewer settled empirical applications. Moderately mature, probably slightly early compared with older candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the recognition window fits 2026 or later.
Large empirical impact is less established than theoretical impact.
Credit allocation among Kamenica, Gentzkow, Bergemann and Morris.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underpins how central banks model inflation, output and policy rules, with a very large influence on practical monetary policy design. It is arguably one of the dominant organising frameworks in macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Highly diffuse. Calvo (pricing), Taylor (rules and staggered contracts), Woodford (synthesis and welfare analysis), Gali and Gertler (Phillips curve and policy), and Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets (estimated DSGE models) all have strong claims. A three-name cap forces arbitrary exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Developed from the 1980s to the 2000s and widely used by institutions. Mature, although the 2008 crisis and the 2021-22 inflation episode prompted reassessment.
uncertainties: Attribution is the main obstacle and no three-person selection is clearly right.
Empirical performance during crises and recent inflation is debated.
Overlap with prior recognition of rational expectations and macroeconomic policy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the long-run impact of policies and schools. The results have shaped research and policy on opportunity and have introduced new empirical standards.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the leading figure across the programme. Hendren and Friedman are central co-authors on neighbourhood and teacher-value-added work, while Katz is credited here as well as in the labour entry for earlier work, and is left out of this proposal.
assessment.maturity: Principal results date from about 2014 to 2022, so the work is relatively recent and follow-up replication, external validity and long-run tracking are still unfolding.
uncertainties: Probably premature relative to other candidates, since much of the work is under a decade old.
Debates about causal interpretation of place effects and about data access limiting independent replication.
Whether credit should be concentrated on Chetty alone.
